# Nativele

> Designed for AI agents. Driven by TypeScript. Defined in vanilla HTML. A lightweight library for building web components: bind HTML templates to TypeScript custom elements. HTML describes structure and where data goes; TypeScript owns state and behavior; the DOM is the only view. Fully typed by tsc, no virtual DOM, no bundler required.

Workflow: write `x.html` + `x.ts`, run `npx ts-dom check` (regenerates `x.html.ts`, runs tsc, or vue-tsc when the project has it, and lint, points errors at the template). Import a template as `import tpl from "./x.html.js"` (note the `.js`). Lint with `npx ts-dom lint` (add `--a11y`). `npx ts-dom rules` lists every rule id. Every diagnostic is `file:line:col severity [rule-id] message` and ends with a `Fix:` hint: read the hint and apply it.

## Template syntax (HTML only names things; no expressions)
- `{{ name }}`: text hole, a single identifier only. NOT `{{ a.b }}` / `{{ a + 1 }}`. Not allowed in attributes.
- `data-ref="x"`: element available as `this.refs.x` (typed by tag).
- `data-if="x"`: hidden by default (the element is REMOVED from the DOM, replaced by a comment); shown when state/props/derive `x` is truthy (or `this.show("x", true)`).
- `<template data-each="items"><li>...</li></template>`: list with exactly one root element; fill it with `this.lists.items.replace(array, item => item.id, (item, { text, refs, show, el }) => {...})`. Not nestable; no `<slot>`, no `data-if` on the root.
- `data-on-<event>="method"`: calls the public method `method(e: Event, hit: EventHit)` on the component. Method name only (no calls). Event name lowercase. Inside a list item `hit.key` is the item key, also for events emitted by a child component placed in the item. Do not name a method like a DOM/ts-dom member (`remove`, `click`, `focus`, `set`, `render`, ...).
- `<slot name="x">`: Light DOM by default (library moves children); native with `shadow: true`.
- `<style>` must be top-level in the HTML file; `<style scoped>` limits it to the component (Light DOM).
- Using another component: just write its tag (`<form-field data-ref="f" label="Name" data-on-field-input="onName">`); the generated module imports it automatically.

## Component (TypeScript)
```ts
import { Component, define, event } from "@nativele/ts-dom";
import type { EmitEvent, EventHit } from "@nativele/ts-dom";
import tpl from "./counter.html.js";

class MyCounter extends Component(tpl, {
  state: { count: 0 },                         // owned by the component, change ONLY with this.set()
  props: { step: 1 },                          // owned by the parent, read-only here (string/number/boolean default => settable from an HTML attribute `step="2"`)
  derive: { double: (s) => s.count * 2 },      // recomputed after every change; usable by {{ double }} / data-if
  emits: { "count-change": event<{ count: number }>() },   // events this component sends up (do not bubble by default)
  // shadow: true,                             // optional Shadow DOM
}) {
  inc() {                                      // referenced by data-on-click="inc"
    this.set((s) => ({ count: s.count + this.props.step }));
    this.emit("count-change", { count: this.state.count });
  }
  override render(view, changed) { /* only for what automatic binding cannot do: lists, attributes, focus */ }
}
define("my-counter", MyCounter);
```
Rules the compiler enforces: every `{{ hole }}` / `data-if` name must exist in state, props or derive (error `missingStateKeys`); state/props/derive names must be unique (`conflictingKeys`); a prop must not be named like an HTMLElement/ts-dom member such as `title`, `hidden`, `render` (`reservedPropNames`); emitted event names must not be native events (`nativeEventNames`); every `data-on-*` method must exist as a public method (`missingHandlers`, reported by `define()`).

## Data flow (one direction)
- `state`, `props`, `render`'s `view` and `derive` arguments are `DeepReadonly`: changing an object or array inside them is a tsc error. Replace with new objects (`s.items.map((i) => (i.id === id ? { ...i, done: true } : i))`). Annotate with read-only types (`readonly Item[]`, `DeepReadonly<State>`).
- State: changed only by its owner with `this.set(patch | s => patch)`; no change => no render. `this.batch(fn)` merges several updates. Rendering is synchronous.
- Props go DOWN: the parent sets them with an attribute or a property (`this.refs.child.value = v.x`, typed). A component never assigns its own props; to ask for a change it `emit`s an event.
- Events go UP: `emit` does not bubble; the parent handles it with `data-on-<event>` on the child tag, casting with `EmitEvent<Child, "event-name">`.
- Data needed several levels away: share a `createStore` module and `this.bind(store, fn)`; do not forward props or re-emit events through middle components (lint rules `prop-forwarding`, `emit-forwarding`).
- `store.set` REPLACES the value (a component's `this.set` merges): `store.set((s) => ({ ...s, status: "loading" }))`. In a component with state/props/derive every `{{ hole }}` must be one of them, so copy store data into state in the `bind` callback: `this.bind(store, (s) => this.set({ total: s.items.length }))`.
- Loading/error states, modal dialogs (a public `open()` called through a typed ref), form validation messages, filtered lists: `docs/recipes.md` and `examples/recipes/` in the repository.
- Writing form values back (lint rule `unguarded-input-value`): only assign `input.value` when it differs (`if (input.value !== v.value) input.value = v.value`), otherwise the caret jumps.

## Minimal example
```html
<!-- counter.html -->
<p>Count: {{ count }} (double: {{ double }})</p>
<button type="button" data-on-click="inc">+1</button>
<p data-if="big">A lot!</p>
```
```ts
// counter.ts
import { Component, define } from "@nativele/ts-dom";
import tpl from "./counter.html.js";
class MyCounter extends Component(tpl, {
  state: { count: 0 },
  derive: { double: (s) => s.count * 2, big: (s) => s.count >= 10 },
}) {
  inc() { this.set((s) => ({ count: s.count + 1 })); }
}
define("my-counter", MyCounter);
```

## Template without a component
`const view = tpl.instantiate()` returns `{ root: DocumentFragment, rootElement, refs, lists, text, show }` typed like a component (`rootElement` exists in the type only when the template has exactly one top-level element, `<style>` excluded), for pieces created in code. No host: `data-on-*` is inert (use `refs.x.addEventListener`) and `<slot>` is not projected.

## Lists
- Rule: an item with anything of its own (state, events, a nested list) is a component filled with `items =`; an item of a few texts and `data-if` is plain elements filled with `replace()`.
- Subscribe in `connected()`, never in the constructor: without `moveBefore` a moved item is disconnected (its `bind`/`on`/`onCleanup` released) and connected again. Data every item needs goes in a `createStore` the item binds.
- Full example (add, remove, sort, toggle, child emit): `examples/readme/task-board.ts` and `task-row.ts` in the repository.
- Items that are components: `<template data-each="todos" data-key="id" data-prop="todo"><todo-row></todo-row></template>`, then `this.lists.todos.items = view.todos` (inside `render`, guarded by `changed.has("todos")`; `changed` holds the state, prop and derived names that changed, so a derived list is guarded by its own name). Keeps the element of each key, creates and removes the rest, sets the `todo` prop of each changed item; `hit.key` in handlers (`hit: EventHit<Todo, "id">` types `hit.key` and `hit.item`). The item component declares `todo` in its `props`; `tsc` checks the items against that prop type and the `data-key` field; an item component defined in a scanned folder must be exported and listed in `ts-dom-tags.ts` (run `ts-dom gen`), otherwise the assignment is a type error that names the problem.
- Items that are plain elements: `<template data-each="x">` with `this.lists.x.replace(items, keyFn, (item, { text, show }) => ...)`.
- `data-each` is never nested: a list inside an item is the item component's own `data-each`.

## Rules for agents
- Skills: `npx ts-dom skills` lists the task procedures shipped with the package (`nativele-core` for building components, `nativele-react`, `nativele-vue`, `nativele-svelte` and `nativele-angular` for those frameworks, `nativele-vite` for Vite, `nativele-integration` for other frameworks, `nativele-state-management`, `nativele-testing`, `nativele-tanstack-query`, `nativele-zod` and `nativele-tailwind` for those tools, `nativele-architecture` for laying out an app with several pages, `nativele-typescript`, `nativele-linting`, `nativele-formatting` and `nativele-ci` for the tsconfig, the linter, the formatter and CI, `nativele-monorepo` for a workspace of several packages, ...), each with verified versions; `npx ts-dom skills <name>` prints one, `npx ts-dom skills add <name>` copies it into `.claude/skills/` or `.agents/skills/`, and `npx ts-dom doctor` suggests the ones that match the project's dependencies.
- `npx ts-dom rules --explain=<id>` (or `rules --json`) explains any rule id from a diagnostic: why it exists, a wrong example and the fix.
- Markup well-formedness is a formatter's job: `oxfmt --check` reports misnested tags that the library's parser would silently repair. Generate with `--whitespace=collapse` when a formatter is used: it keeps only the whitespace the browser renders, judged by each element's default display as formatters judge it, so reformatting a template changes neither the page nor `textContent` (a `<div>` restyled `display: inline` still counts as a block: use an inline tag for inline content).
- If checks behave oddly (no types, a template not found), run `npx ts-dom doctor --json` first: it reports tsconfig, import path, runtime, generated file and plugin problems with a `Fix:` each (`--project=<path>` picks the tsconfig, `--strict` also fails on warnings).
- `npx ts-dom gen --check` (writes nothing, exit 1) tells whether the generated files are stale before you trust `tsc` errors.
- Never edit `x.html.ts` or `ts-dom-tags.ts` (generated). After any `.html` or component change run `npx ts-dom check --json`: it regenerates, runs tsc, maps template contract errors to the template line/col (`missing-binding`, `missing-handler`, item rules), and runs lint. Fix every issue by its `Fix:` hint; never cast a type error away.
- No expressions in HTML; computed values go in `derive`. Change state only with `this.set()`. Lists, attributes and focus go in `render(view, changed)`; check `changed.has("items")` before rebuilding a list, and annotate `changed` with the names you check (`ReadonlySet<"items" | "visible">`), not `ReadonlySet<string>`, so tsc checks them.
- Props go down (parent sets them), events go up (`emit`, handled with `data-on-<event>` on the child tag). `data-each` cannot be nested: make the inner list its own component.

## Setup
```sh
npm i -D typescript && npm i @nativele/ts-dom
npx ts-dom gen && npx tsc          # tsconfig: module/moduleResolution NodeNext (or bundler), lib includes DOM, strict true (required on TypeScript 5; 6 and 7 only reject false)
```
In a browser without a bundler map the bare name once: `<script type="importmap">{"imports":{"@nativele/ts-dom":"/node_modules/@nativele/ts-dom/dist/index.mjs"}}</script>`; relative imports in your own code need `.js` extensions. With Vite, `@nativele/ts-dom/vite` is optional.

## Pitfalls
- Import templates with `./x.html.js`, not `./x.html`. Run `ts-dom gen` before `tsc` (it creates `x.html.ts` and `ts-dom-tags.ts`; both are generated, do not edit or commit).
- Exports: `export class` the component to get typed `refs.child` in parent templates (`define("tag", Class)` is scanned).
- `data-if` content is hidden until the name is truthy (it stays in memory, so its `refs` still work); `{{ hole }}` stays empty until filled.
- With Vite, `package.json` needs `"type": "module"`.
- `slotchange()` is Light-DOM only; with `shadow: true` use the native `slotchange` event.
- A Light DOM component builds its content when connected (a `shadow: true` one in the constructor), so a new Light element has no children, `refs` or `text` until it is appended.
- Inside a framework (React, Vue, Svelte, ...), children the framework later inserts, removes or reorders in a Light DOM host with slots break or land in the wrong slot: use `shadow: true`, or one stable element per slot.
